C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION.IntentSummary: Introduce a reviewable, fail-closed release-preparation pipeline for Mark: a checked-in train manifest is the deterministic authority, GitHub Projects mirrors operational state, a pinned Release Please CLI prepares but never publishes, governance/readiness checks verify the payload-to-seal boundary and all user-facing materials, and separate signing/publication approvals plus rulesets preserve owner-authorized release control.
C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION.ExecutionPolicy: Implement in dependency-aware waves. Repository validators and fixtures land before any GitHub setting is applied. Release preparation produces a product payload commit; a later metadata-only freeze commit records payloadSha and seals the reviewed evidence without pretending a commit can contain its own SHA. Every external apply command is idempotent, supports dry-run/read-back, uses a purpose-specific least-privilege credential, and is never part of a tag or publication instruction. The existing dirty working tree must be partitioned so unrelated FIX-013, Windows titlebar, and other active-bundle changes are not staged accidentally.

MustPassCommand.Command: npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js tests/renderer/release-materials.test.js tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js tests/renderer/release-project-sync.test.js tests/renderer/release-github-controls.test.js tests/renderer/release-notes.test.js tests/renderer/whatsNew/content.test.js

Gate.Name: train-and-materials
Gate.Command: npm run release:materials -- --tag v2.6.0 && npm run release:readiness -- --tag v2.6.0 --payload PAYLOAD_SHA
Gate.Expect: Exact payloadSha, metadata-only payload-to-seal delta, unambiguous user-facing/operational/not-present scope, owner acceptance, required check evidence, ten source locales plus minified parity, README/CHANGELOG/notes/in-app consistency, tracked README PNGs, and matching SHA-256 screenshot digests; emits BLOCK_RELEASE_MATERIALS_CONSISTENT and BLOCK_RELEASE_READINESS_CONFIRMED.

Gate.Name: focused-regressions
Gate.Command: npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js tests/renderer/release-materials.test.js tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js tests/renderer/release-project-sync.test.js tests/renderer/release-github-controls.test.js tests/renderer/release-notes.test.js tests/renderer/whatsNew/content.test.js tests/renderer/whatsNew/gate.test.js
Gate.Expect: Positive fixtures pass; each missing/stale/ambiguous condition named in the spec fails independently with a stable error code.

Gate.Name: release-preparation-dry-run
Gate.Expect: Reads the Release Please package/manifest version, reports the remaining Cargo/Tauri/fixture/material identities it would change without writing, tagging, publishing, or contacting GitHub; a pinned Release Please dry-run independently computes 2.6.0 from the current Conventional Commit history.

Gate.Name: github-controls-dry-run
Gate.Command: npm run release:project-sync -- --dry-run && npm run release:github-controls -- --dry-run
Gate.Expect: Reports Project field/item, Environment, main ruleset, and v* tag ruleset deltas without external mutation; no token value is logged.

Gate.Name: github-controls-read-back
Gate.Expect: Authenticated API read-back matches source-controlled configuration after separately authorized apply; temporary Projects API failure is reported as mirror drift and never changes the repository gate decision.

Gate.Name: workflow-boundary
Gate.Expect: AST-level checks prove Release Please cannot tag/publish; manual dispatch cannot sign/publish; event values reach shell only through validated environment variables; an existing tag is peeled and bound to the checked-out seal; release/readiness precedes every packaging action; signing and publication jobs use their contracted Environments; permissions are job-scoped; actions are immutable-SHA pinned; no publication occurs on merge of the preparation PR.

Gate.Name: governance
Gate.Command: grace lint --path . --assertions current && grace status --path . --with modules --json
Gate.Expect: Zero GRACE errors; M-046/V-M-046 and M-011/V-M-011 describe the implemented release and in-app-material surfaces.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add docs/release-trains/2.5.x-next.json with schema-versioned train identity, lifecycle state, previous release, Release Please computedVersion, exact payloadSha, included user-facing items, included operational items, explicit not-present exclusions, owner-acceptance evidence, integration commits, required checks, materials, and dated transitions.

Define Collecting → Preparing → Frozen → Ready → Released or Aborted. Release-preparation merges all product/material bytes first; a later seal commit records payloadSha and changes only the train JSON/Markdown plus screenshot manifest. The tag points to the seal commit, never to payloadSha.

Validation rejects duplicate or ambiguous membership, user-facing items without acceptance, a commit in v2.5.3..payloadSha that is not classified, an exclusion whose code is present without operational admission, invalid lifecycle transitions, a non-ancestor payload, any non-allowlisted payload-to-seal change, and any mismatch between requested version/payload and the frozen manifest.
The Markdown train remains the human ledger and links to the JSON authority; a deterministic sync/check reports drift instead of silently choosing one side.

T-002.Title: Release materials and screenshot identity gate

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add release-materials validation for the Release Please generated CHANGELOG, the first README release section, the English GitHub-notes draft, the in-app data entry, all ten canonical locale files and their minified derivatives, release URLs, item ordering/count, footer/Also copy, and existing title/text length limits. Every visible CHANGELOG entry maps to an admitted user-facing or explicitly named operational commit; Conventional Commit policy keeps future internal-only work out of feat/fix sections.

Parse both Markdown images and HTML img/source references. Add docs/assets/readme/2.6.0.manifest.json with schema version, release version, payloadSha, exact README_SHOTS capture command, reviewed date/reviewer/scenarios, and the exact README-referenced PNG set with lowercase SHA-256 digests; reject missing, extra, untracked, or digest-mismatched images.

Add a deterministic release-notes extractor/composer so the reviewed v2.6.0 English draft is used when the draft GitHub Release is created, above the generated verification block; publication never starts with notes the gate ignored.

The screenshot manifest proves which reviewed bytes will ship; visual composition, product correctness, and native-copy quality remain explicit human review evidence and are never inferred from hashes, key presence, or character counts.

Verification.Command: npm run release:materials -- --tag v2.6.0 && npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-materials.test.js tests/renderer/whatsNew/content.test.js tests/renderer/whatsNew/gate.test.js

T-003.Title: Release Please bootstrap, Conventional SemVer, and PR normalization

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Configure an exact locked Release Please CLI version in manifest mode for root package '.', include-component-in-tag=false, include-v-in-tag=true, always-update=true and skip-github-release=true. Seed manifest version 2.5.3 and bootstrap-sha 0ed3351ec30aa7b9d9c166bdb4133149e4dd88e6: that commit must remain on main ancestry and its tree must equal tagged v2.5.3 commit acad9988220c9a1a6d28ea4e94b69d69d774f805, otherwise bootstrap fails.

Release Please exclusively owns computed SemVer, .release-please-manifest.json, package.json, both package-lock version fields and CHANGELOG.md. Standard Conventional Commit inference owns the next version; the current feat history must dry-run to exactly 2.6.0 without --release-as or another manual override, and the first generated CHANGELOG layout is an explicit acceptance artifact before activation.

Add a required Conventional Commit/PR-title check: fix is patch, feat is minor, and ! or BREAKING CHANGE is major; feat is reserved for user-visible/product-contract additions, internal tooling uses chore/test/ci/docs. Ruleset merge policy ensures the conventional title reaching main is the one Release Please reads.

Add a dependency-free release-normalize tool that refuses an explicit target version, reads and cross-checks the Release Please package/manifest version, then structurally updates only Cargo.toml workspace version, the mark package in Cargo.lock, tauri.conf.json, intended positive M-046 fixture locations and version-bound README/What's New/locale/release-note paths/URLs. It never calculates SemVer or rewrites CHANGELOG; historical/negative fixtures are untouched, a golden diff pins the exact patch, the second run is byte-empty, and check mode never writes.

Use a purpose-specific GitHub App/fine-grained bot token with contents and pull-request rights only so the generated PR triggers checks. After Release Please opens/updates it, a trusted default-branch workflow checks out that returned PR head, runs release:normalize --write, commits the exact normalization patch as chore(release), and proves all checks run on the final head.

Neither merging the preparation PR nor running its workflow creates a tag, GitHub Release, deployment, store upload, cask change, Environment/ruleset mutation, or Project-administration mutation. The next preparation PR cannot merge while the previous prepared version remains untagged/unpublished without an explicit Aborted transition.

The preparation PR runs release preflight, material/governance checks and focused tests, and reports that payloadSha, screenshot review/digests and the seal commit are created only after merge and green payload CI.

Verification.Command: npm run release:normalize -- --check && npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-normalize.test.js tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js tests/renderer/release-github-controls.test.js

T-004.Title: Required governance/readiness checks and exact ref binding

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add an event/mode matrix. Ordinary PR/main runs stable release/governance for schemas, source-controlled controls and tests without demanding a frozen train. A release-preparation/freeze PR runs prospective checks. Frozen main and tag contexts run strict release/readiness over payloadSha, the allowlisted seal delta, acceptance, exact diff accounting, materials and screenshot digests.

Tag-push is the only production path. Manual dispatch is build-only and cannot reach signing or publication. The tag path validates strict SemVer through an environment variable, requires an existing remote tag, and proves github.ref_type=tag, github.ref_name=TAG, the peeled tag commit, checked-out HEAD and release seal commit are identical before any package step.

The offline CLI deterministically aggregates version/tag preflight, frozen-train validation, payload/seal identity, owner acceptance records, exact diff accounting, material consistency, screenshot digests and source-controlled control validation with stable path-free diagnostics. The online strict Actions wrapper additionally queries exact expected check contexts for payloadSha and fails on missing, failed, wrong-SHA, or wrong-App results; checked-in green claims are never treated as live proof.

The offline gate is repository-only. GitHub Projects availability never affects either decision, while the Checks API is a distinct mandatory dependency for online freeze/tag admission. Negative tests cover branch dispatch with publish intent, missing/nonexistent/wrong-target tags, payload/seal mismatch, metacharacter input, a product-code seal delta, absent/stale check runs, Projects outage, and a release context attempting the ordinary N/A mode.

Verification.Command: npm run release:governance && npm run release:readiness -- --tag v2.6.0 --payload PAYLOAD_SHA && npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Source-control ownerType=user, owner login, Project title, visibility, and typed Train, Admission, Owner acceptance, Payload SHA, Release state, Item ID, and public Evidence URL field contracts. A dedicated train-summary item owns train-level state; change items sync by stable item ID.

Bootstrap queries user(login), follows GraphQL cursors, then records the Project number/node ID after explicit owner apply. Reconcile is one-way manifest → Project, overwrites only owned fields, preserves unowned fields, rejects zero/multiple rows for one stable ID, and never automatically deletes fields/items or reverse-syncs Project edits into release authority.

The CLI/workflow supports offline dry-run, bootstrap/apply and read-back; uses concurrency plus bounded retry/resume; repeated apply performs zero mutations. Pagination, duplicate ID, partial failure, option migration and unowned-field preservation have deterministic fixtures.

Use a dedicated expiring PROJECT_MIRROR_AUTH credential with only the required user-Project scopes in a push-main/manual sync job, never on pull_request or pull_request_target. Missing scopes/outage produce visible non-required mirror drift without weakening readiness; public-field allowlisting rejects machine paths, private notes and private evidence URLs.

Verification.Command: npm run release:project-sync -- --dry-run && npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-project-sync.test.js

T-006.Title: Approved automatic tag, tag-only signing, and draft-first publication

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A trusted promote-release workflow starts only for the merged freeze result (with an input-free owner recovery dispatch), creates a pending release-authorize deployment, and derives version/SHA solely from the checked-out Ready seal. After owner approval, a purpose-specific Release Bot App token with contents:write only creates one annotated v<computedVersion> tag at that exact commit; rejection/timeout creates nothing, and rerun is no-op only when the existing tag target matches.

The promoter must use the GitHub App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN, so the tag push starts release.yml. The tag workflow rejects any tag whose target, annotation, version, actor/path or Ready seal evidence is wrong; out-of-band tag pushes cannot enter signing or publication.

Manual release workflow_dispatch remains unsigned build-only. Only the bot-created pushed v* tag with exact tag/seal identity can enter production signing. APPLE_* and TAURI signing/updater secrets move from repository scope to the tag-restricted release-signing Environment; no branch, pull request, arbitrary manual ref, or mismatched tag can access them.

Reuse the existing release Environment for the job that creates/promotes the GitHub Release, with xronocode as required reviewer and prevent_self_review=false because this is a single-owner repository. This is an explicit second confirmation, not independent review. The cask job depends on successful publication and uses its own narrowly scoped bot-secret boundary without a duplicate owner approval.

After approval, create or reconcile one draft release with --verify-tag, upload the exact expected asset inventory, verify server read-back/digests/latest.json and reviewed human notes, then promote draft=false as the final GitHub publication step. An injected failure leaves only a draft and never advances /latest; reruns converge on that draft; a published release is never asset-clobbered.

Enable/read-back immutable releases if supported for this repository and document the notes-only correction path. Refuse to overwrite, delete, or retarget a published release/tag during automated recovery.

Set repository Actions default to read. Workflow-level permissions are empty/read-only; build/readiness get contents:read only plus narrowly needed attestation OIDC on the relevant job, publish alone gets contents:write, and privileged actions in release/release-please/governance workflows are pinned to verified full commit SHAs with automated dependency-review updates.

T-007.Title: Staged GitHub control-plane bootstrap and rulesets

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Split credentials and commands: release:project-sync uses PROJECT_MIRROR_AUTH; release:github-controls defaults to read-only/dry-run and may apply only from an explicit owner-authenticated local admin session. No reusable repository-admin PAT is stored in Actions and CI refuses admin apply.

Source-control stable managed names and exact desired Environment/default-permission/main-ruleset/v*-tag-ruleset definitions. Main requires stable aggregate CI plus release/governance, blocks force-push/delete and keeps an explicit owner recovery actor; tag rules restrict v* create/update/delete to the documented release path without a broad always-bypass role.

Apply is staged and non-destructive: export current state, create/update only managed resources in evaluate mode when available (otherwise disabled/manual activation), GET/read-back each mutation, append a local journal with resource IDs and payload digests, stop on first mismatch, run PR/tag canaries, then require a separate owner activation. Unknown resources and existing Environments are never automatically deleted.

Rollback works out-of-band even when pushes are blocked: restore the captured managed-resource payload or disable/evaluate it in reverse journal order. Environment migration never assumes secret values can be read or copied; read-back verifies reviewer, self-review, deployment-ref policy, default workflow permissions, ruleset bypasses and exact required check sources.

Verification.Command: npm run release:github-controls -- --dry-run && npm run release:github-controls -- --check && npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-github-controls.test.js

T-008.Title: Lifecycle, recovery, GRACE contracts, and final four-angle review

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Document Collecting → Preparing → Frozen → Ready → Released and explicit Aborted transitions. Any membership/runtime/material mutation from Frozen/Ready returns to Collecting and clears payload/check/digest readiness while preserving historical acceptance unless behavior changed. A rejected approval is an attempt failure, not automatic Aborted; Released/Aborted are terminal and start a new immutable train ID.

Document preparation-PR failure, an untagged merged preparation, stale payload, rejected signing/publication approval, Projects outage/scope failure, partial GitHub-control apply, draft-release upload failure, post-promotion failure and Homebrew-only failure. Post-tag attempts and per-channel outcomes are append-only; accepted/queued/frozen/ready never means release authorization.

Update M-046/V-M-046 for train, materials, governance/readiness, GitHub controls, security boundaries and stable markers; update M-011/V-M-011 only for in-app What's New content/gates. File-local contracts/maps/change summaries match actual responsibilities.

Run independent correctness/data-integrity, security/permissions, operations/recovery, and product/materials reviews; resolve every blocking finding and record remaining non-blocking risks before owner implementation acceptance.

Verification.Command: grace lint --path . --assertions current && grace status --path . --with modules --json && git diff --check

Corner.name: Correctness and data integrity
Corner.Expected: Release Please is the SemVer/CHANGELOG authority; the checked-in train manifest is the admission authority; payload/seal/material identities are exact; Project state is a one-way operational mirror; every negative condition has an isolated regression fixture.

Corner.name: Security and authorization
Corner.Expected: Preparation cannot publish; owner-approved tag automation has no free-form target; build jobs are read-only; signing secrets are tag-restricted; publication requires a second owner confirmation; rulesets prevent accidental main/tag bypass; tokens are purpose-specific and never logged.

Corner.name: Operations and recovery
Corner.Expected: Every external mutation has dry-run, idempotent apply, read-back, and rollback/recovery instructions; Project outage does not weaken admission while exact check-run API failure blocks online release; stale payloads and failed post-tag runs have explicit state transitions.

Corner.name: Product and release materials
Corner.Expected: README, CHANGELOG, release notes, in-app sheet, ten locales, and reviewed screenshots describe only frozen accepted scope; hashes prove reviewed image identity but never replace visual acceptance.

Corner.name: Performance
Corner.Expected: Offline readiness and the small online check-run query finish before expensive packaging; hash work is bounded to referenced PNGs; no runtime code path or application startup cost is introduced.

Corner.name: Portability
Corner.Expected: Node tools use cross-platform paths and LF-tolerant parsing; release-readiness runs on Linux/macOS/Windows checkout semantics without machine-specific paths.

Corner.name: Scope discipline
Corner.Expected: No version bump, candidate freeze, tag, release, store upload, cask publication, or GitHub setting mutation occurs during planning or without its separately authorized apply/release step.

Review.Findings: Correctness/data integrity: replaced the impossible self-referential candidate SHA with payloadSha plus a metadata-only seal; split ordinary governance from strict freeze/tag readiness; bound existing tag, peeled commit, checkout and seal; made Release Please the Conventional Commit SemVer and CHANGELOG authority, with a one-time 2.5.3 divergent-history bootstrap and structural PR-head normalization for Cargo/Tauri/lock/test surfaces. Security/permissions: removed manual publish/ref input, added owner-approved input-free bot tag creation, tag-only signing secrets, a separate protected draft-first publication step, read-only defaults, job-scoped permissions, immutable action pins, no asset clobber and local-only admin apply. Operations/recovery: made Projects a paginated one-way user-owned mirror with its own token; split it from admin controls; added staged ruleset activation, per-resource read-back/journaling/rollback, explicit lifecycle invalidation and per-channel recovery. Product/materials: the generated CHANGELOG, README, reviewed notes, in-app sheet, ten canonical/minified locales and fresh HTML/Markdown-referenced PNGs are cross-checked; screenshot hashes prove reviewed bytes while visual/native-language quality remains human evidence. Current history computes 2.6.0 rather than the previously drafted 2.5.4. No implementation, GitHub mutation, version bump, tag or publication occurred.
